title: Chapter 266: Stay a Little While Longer
html:
Dressed as the deranged doctor and carrying his fearsome hammer, Chen Ge stood at the first junction. This time, he had entered not to rescue visitors but to exploit the Haunted House’s environment and capture the two suspected Ghost Stories Society members. Where did they go?

Chen Ge stood silently and listened. Before long, a sound came from the corridor leading to the Deep Well. A human head rolled toward him, propelled by an unseen force.

“Out playing again?” Chen Ge approached the mannequin head. He assumed it had lost its body and rolled out in search of help. Before he could reach it, however, the head turned down another passage, moving at precisely the speed needed for him to follow.

“You’re going to be my guide?”

Chen Ge followed without hesitation. A draft stirred his bloodied doctor’s coat as the skin-masked figure carried his enormous red hammer behind the rolling head, deeper into the Haunted House.

…

Yang Chen’s heart leaped at the sight of Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming. Whether they were visitors or employees, their arrival could only help.

“You just came out of there?” Wei Wu regarded the students coldly. Having sensed the threat, he no longer cared to maintain his disguise.

“Yes.” Yang Chen wanted to ask for help, but Wei Wu’s manner made him uneasy. No service employee should address customers with such hostility.

“What did you find? What happened to all three of you?” Kong Xiangming joined them. The questions baffled the students, who had assumed the pair were Haunted House employees.

Are these two really clueless about the layout of the Haunted House, or are they toying with us?

Before the students could decide, Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming suddenly turned toward the glass door of Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy in perfect unison.

“What are you looking at?” Uneasy, Yang Chen retreated toward his friends. The situation was more complicated than he had thought. Two seconds later, the glass door opened by itself and a faint stench drifted out.

“Besides those mannequins, other souls are trapped inside this Haunted House. How unexpected.” Wei Wu spoke quietly. They would never expose themselves to outsiders unless necessary.

“Mine has already awakened, and it’s hungry.” A pair of arms curled over Kong Xiangming’s shoulders, followed by a shrunken head climbing from his back.

“Have you lost your mind? There are witnesses!” Wei Wu tried to stop him, but the medical students had already seen everything.

“I cannot control it when it’s hungry.” Kong Xiangming sounded calm, as though this had happened many times. “It doesn’t matter if they see. We’ll dispose of them as well, though wasting these identities is unfortunate.”

Wei Wu had not expected the normally reserved Kong Xiangming to act so decisively.

“Fine. Mine is hungry too.” Blood vessels writhed across the back of Wei Wu’s head. He turned toward the students, only to find no fear on their faces—merely expressions that said, We knew it.

“They aren’t afraid?” Wei Wu had no idea what the students had endured. Compared with the hidden scenario, the members’ monsters looked almost adorable.

“I’ll leave these three to you.” Kong Xiangming entered Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy alone. In the darkness, something else seemed to crawl from his back. The students watched him disappear, each wearing a different expression.

“Should we warn him?” Li Xue felt sorry for the man.

“Stop worrying about him, these two have to be employees.”

When visitors saw a ghost inside a Haunted House, they naturally assumed it was an employee. Wang Dan used the wall to pull himself upright. Though frightened, he had recovered some of his usual tone.

He sighed and stumbled toward Wei Wu. “We surrender. Please take us out.”

A face had nearly formed on the back of Wei Wu’s head, but Wang Dan’s request halted the transformation. “You want me to lead you out?”

“Yes, the three of us have given up already.”

What is happening?Wei Wu had created numerous ghost stories to fulfill the society’s demands. His victims normally lost the ability to speak the moment they saw his true form.

“Let’s go.” Wang Dan’s legs trembled. Holding his head with one hand, he seized Wei Wu’s arm with the other. “Sir, can we leave now? My head is spinning, and we have class this afternoon.”

Wei Wu tried and failed to shake him loose. “Are you blind? Can’t you see the bloody face on the back of my head? Show some respect!”

“We already surrendered. What else do you want?” Wang Dan snapped. The day had stripped away most of his confidence and pride.

Wei Wu decided something was wrong with the students. Whatever the cause, he would end this quickly. “None of you will be leaving.”

The blood vessels wove themselves into a terrifying, indistinct face that slowly assumed Wang Dan’s likeness.

“Can you stop with the tricks? We’re exhausted after that hidden scenario. Keep this up, and I’ll leave a negative review online.” Wang Dan’s head throbbed, but holding Wei Wu’s arm made him feel oddly secure.

“What are you talking about?” Wei Wu summoned enough strength to shove him away. Both his faces wore the same murderous expression. “We planned to finish this quickly, but now…”

Wind surged through the corridor. Halfway through the sentence, the face behind Wei Wu screamed.

Wei Wu turned and saw a monster in bloodstained clothes charging behind a rolling human head, an enormous hammer in its hands.

Wei Wu’s scalp went numb as an overwhelming sense of danger seized him. “This is bad!”

He instinctively turned to flee toward Kong Xiangming, but the ‘monster’ gave him no chance.

“You’ve only just arrived. Why the rush to leave?”
